Threat.value: I avoid going to unfamiliar places because I cannot assess the danger
I watch other people closely for signs that they might harm me
I find it harder to feel safe at night than during the day

Memory.value: There are parts of the event that I simply cannot remember no matter how hard I try
When the memory comes back it feels completely real across all my senses at once
Fragments of the memory appear suddenly without warning and then disappear

Negative Appraisals.value: The people or institutions that should have protected me let me down

vignette: Rohan had always been a free spirit, his music taking him to new and exciting places. But that all changed when he was stalked by an obsessive fan. The experience left him shaken, and over time, he began to feel like he was losing himself in the process of trying to stay safe. As he reflected on what had happened, Rohan couldn't help but think that he was a weak person for not being able to protect himself. He felt dead inside, as if the music that once brought him so much joy was now just a hollow echo of its former self. These feelings of weakness and numbness only intensified his fear of unfamiliar places, making it difficult for him to venture out into new environments without feeling like he was walking into danger. Watching others closely became second nature, as he searched for signs that they might be a threat. The memories of the stalking were fragmented, with pieces appearing suddenly without warning, only to disappear just as quickly. Rohan found himself trying to fill in the gaps, but it was like trying to grasp at smoke - the harder he tried, the more elusive the truth became. When the memories did surface, they came back with a vengeance, flooding his senses and making him feel like he was reliving the experience all over again. Rohan's perceptions of danger were heightened by these sudden recollections, making it even harder for him to feel safe at night. He would lie awake, listening for any sign that someone might be lurking outside his window, his mind racing with worst-case scenarios. This hypervigilance only served to reinforce his negative appraisals, solidifying in his mind the notion that he was a weak person who couldn't even protect himself. As Rohan struggled to make sense of what had happened, he couldn't shake the feeling that the institutions that were supposed to keep him safe - the police, the courts - had let him down. This sense of institutional failure only added to his feelings of vulnerability, making it harder for him to trust others and increasing his reliance on his own vigilance. The cumulative effect was a life lived in constant fear, where every new face was a potential threat, and every unfamiliar place was a source of anxiety. Rohan's music, once a source of comfort and expression, now felt like a distant memory, a reminder of the person he used to be before the stalking had taken over his life. As he sat in his small apartment, surrounded by the remnants of a career that seemed to be slipping away from him, Rohan realized that he needed help. He couldn't keep living like this, constantly on edge and unable to trust himself or others. It was time to face the fears and doubts that had been holding him back for so long, and to find a way to reclaim his music - and himself.
